codeql.resolved: Notification custom-client numeric-field HTML injection; newly editor-reachable compiler regex denial of service; generated-baseline checked-path/bounded-read race. All three findings absent from final scan.
codeql.limitations: Remaining results include test fixtures, style findings, intentional Promise identity checks, guarded flows, and pre-existing local filesystem hardening gaps. This is not a zero-finding scan or a security guarantee.

operationalLimits: Linux namespace prerequisites must be validated on the deployment host; the disposable VM does not establish that a hosted nested-container policy permits Bubblewrap. Missing or denied enforcement fails closed.
Process runner remains for trusted applications; Docker provider isolation requires the documented host policy and quota configuration.
Managed canaries currently support local code-only releases; no provider canaries or concurrent schema migration.
PITR uses a bounded, schema-sealed, single-writer epoch and needs independently retained encrypted exports/checkpoints.
Node evacuation is planned maintenance with downtime; unresolved writer-cleanup fences block admission, restore and deletion.
Existing docs search misses hyphenated queries when the index normalized those words to spaces.

Pre-existing backup/CLI pathname races require a concurrent local filesystem adversary; private stable operator-owned paths remain required. Benchmark utilities retain predictable temporary report defaults; use --output in an operator-owned directory. See detailed triage.
